description_full: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V. engages in the ice cream business in the Netherlands. The company offers its products under the Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, and Wall's brands. It also operates in rest of Europe, North America, South America, Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Australia, and New Zealand. The company was incorporated in 2025 and is headquartered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

financial_summary: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N. is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $11.7B market cap on $8.8B of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 234% against a 10% cost of capital — a 224-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $140M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 5.1×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 27% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
